highlights.body: `cmux acp daemon shutdown` now stops only the agent daemon: agents keep running and the next daemon picks them up, the same as a restart or an update. Add `--end-agents` to end every agent too. Before, a plain shutdown ended every agent on the machine, including agents that other windows or other people were using.
highlights.title: Stopping the agent daemon keeps your agents running

highlights.body:
Emulate Device… in the browser's Tools menu (or the palette) shows every device of Chrome's device toolbar, grouped as Chrome groups them, and newer devices that Chrome does not list yet. In a Chromium tab the page gets the device's viewport, pixel ratio, user agent, client hints, touch and mobile layout, as in Chrome's device mode. A WebKit tab gets the viewport, pixel ratio and user agent. Choose an orientation or the unfolded screen of a foldable from the same menu.

Agents and scripts use the same list: `cmux browser devices list`, `cmux tab <tab> emulate --device "iPhone 16 Pro"`, and `cmux browser devices add` for your own devices in Chrome's device format.
highlights.title: Emulate phones, tablets and foldables in the browser

highlights.body: Move Tab to Browser Profile now keeps the tab: same place, same tab, and the page reloads at the same address in the new profile, with that profile's cookies, site data and permissions. Back and forward history starts over in the new profile, and unsaved form input on the page is lost. Agents can create browser profiles, open a tab in one and move a tab to another from the command line: `cmux browser profile create --name Work`, `cmux browser profile open <url> --engine webkit --profile Work` and `cmux browser tab <tab> set-profile --profile Work` (also an MCP tool). Agents cannot delete a profile.
highlights.title: Move a tab to another browser profile without losing its place

highlights.body: When a chat on an SSH machine asks to run a command, Allow now runs it there. Before, the first Allow on that machine did nothing, because its agent service did not hold this Mac's approval key. cmux now gives the key before the chat starts when nothing else runs on that machine's agent service. When other agents run there, cmux asks first: the chat shows a Restart button, and the running agents keep working through the restart.
highlights.title: Allow works for chats on SSH machines

highlights.body: A new chat in an SSH workspace now asks whether you trust its folder on that machine, the same question a chat on this Mac asks. Choose Trust and the chat starts there. Before, the send failed with "not a trusted folder" and the app had no way to answer. New Agent Chat from an SSH workspace also starts in a folder of that workspace on the machine, not with "Open a terminal in a folder first".
highlights.title: Chats on SSH machines ask to trust their folder
